name: record_hypothesis
arguments: {"statement": "R103H is a buried-core substitution in the JAK3 FERM domain. Replacing arginine with histidine removes a side-chain interaction that holds the FERM fold together, so the protein is destabilised or misfolded and degraded, which lowers JAK3 levels and signalling.", "mechanism_class": "stability_folding", "supports": ["E4", "E7", "E12", "E14", "E15", "E16", "E18", "E1", "E10"], "would_refute": "An AlphaFold model or experimental model shows R103 side chain solvent-exposed (relative SASA above about 25%) with no polar or salt-bridge partner, and a stability predictor (e.g. FoldX or Rosetta ddG) gives |ddG| below 1 kcal/mol for R103H.", "starting_rank": 1, "rank_rationale": "Ranked first because the starting evidence on this residue is all indirect but points one way: high conservation (E14 0.898), strongly deleterious predictors (E12 AlphaMissense 0.84, E15 popEVE -3.8, E16 EVE 0.83), a FERM-domain location (E4, E7), and a recessive LOF SCID phenotype (E1, E10). Rank 1 is not strong: G2 and G3 say the residue's structural environment and effect on stability are unknown, and no assay covers R103 (G1, G5). The substitution-specific evidence in E2 (R103C also pathogenic) supports that the residue itself matters, not which mechanism. Missing: per-residue burial or ddG calculation on the AlphaFold model, and any expression or stability data."}

name: record_hypothesis
arguments: {"statement": "R103H folds normally but removes a surface contact that JAK3 needs to couple to the common gamma chain (IL2RG) or other cytokine receptors through its N-terminal FERM region, so receptor association and STAT activation fail.", "mechanism_class": "protein_interaction", "supports": ["E5", "E20", "E10", "E19", "E13"], "would_refute": "In a predicted JAK3 complex with the gamma chain or a cytokine receptor intracellular region (e.g. AlphaFold-Multimer or a docking model), R103 lies more than 10 \u00c5 from any receptor residue, and its buried surface area does not change between wild type and R103H.", "starting_rank": 2, "rank_rationale": "Ranked second because the record ties the FERM N-terminus to receptor binding (E5, a UniProt region annotated for cytokine receptor interaction, though based on sequence similarity) and lists known partners (E20), and E10 shows JAK3 loss of function causes SCID. Still weaker than the folding hypothesis: E5 is inferred by similarity, no retrieved source places residue 103 at a receptor contact (G2, G3), and the gamma-chain association point is unverified. Missing: a receptor-complex model and any co-immunoprecipitation data for R103H."}

name: record_hypothesis
arguments: {"statement": "R103H sits at an intramolecular FERM-SH2 or FERM-kinase interface. Losing the arginine breaks the autoinhibitory or scaffold contact that positions the kinase domain, so catalytic output is reduced.", "mechanism_class": "domain_interface", "supports": ["E8", "E4", "E7", "E11"], "would_refute": "In the AlphaFold model, R103 has no atom within 5 \u00c5 of any SH2 or kinase-domain residue, and the FERM-SH2 and FERM-kinase interface contacts are unchanged when R103H is modelled, so the residue sits outside the inter-domain interface.", "starting_rank": 3, "rank_rationale": "Ranked third because its only support is an analogy: E8 is a crystal structure of the Jak2 FERM-SH2 module, not JAK3, and the interface location of R103 is unverified (G2). E11 is about gain of function from ATP binding, not loss of function, so it does not favour this mechanism. Missing: JAK3 domain-boundary mapping of residue 103 and a comparison of R103 with the Jak2 interface residues after alignment."}
